summary: A guitar chord diagram: strings, frets, finger dots with numbers, open and muted strings, a barre, the position (5fr) and the notes under the strings, from a chord name ("Dm": the server finds a playable shape) or a fingering ("xx0231").

chord.doc: A chord name (Dm, C7, F#m7b5, G/B): the server finds the lowest playable shape with every chord tone, the root (or slash bass) lowest and at most four fingers; also names a fingering

frets.doc: A fingering, low string first: "xx0231" (x muted, 0 open); frets over 9 need separators: "x-x-12-14-15-14". The chord is identified from the notes when chord isn't given

fingers.doc: Finger numbers in the same form ("xx0231" for Dm: 0 or x for none); default: worked out, with a barre when the lowest fret spans several strings

barre.doc: Draw a barre at this fret across the strings that hold it (default: found from the fingers)

labels.doc: Under each sounding string: the note (spelled for the chord), its interval (R, ♭3, 5), or nothing

title.doc: Text above the diagram; default: the chord symbol

tuning.doc: Open strings, low first; default ["E2", "A2", "D3", "G3", "B3", "E4"] (4 for a ukulele: ["G4", "C4", "E4", "A4"])

position.doc: First fret shown (default: the nut, or the lowest fret used when the shape is higher up)

size.doc: Diagram height in dp (the width follows); it shrinks, centred, when the box is smaller

label.doc: Accessibility description; default: the chord and every string

pitfalls: Give the chord name or the fingering, never draw dots yourself; the fingering is low string first (the way chord charts read left to right)
From a name the server picks one shape (open position first, then the lowest barre shape): give frets for a particular voicing

Fingers are worked out when not given: one finger per fret from the lowest, a barre with finger 1 when the lowest fret holds several strings and five or more notes need fingers; give fingers to show your own
The diagram keeps its proportions: inside a smaller box it shrinks, centred, with every label
